ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: "EARLY MUSIC AND ITS MOVEMENTS." The reimagination of European musical premodernity for modern audiences is the cornerstone of the cultural phenomenon referred to as Early Music. And yet this very act of “re-enchantment” is contradictory in nature and its concern with ideas of authenticity has continued to divide opinion. This seminar seeks to reinstate the plurality of movement in the “Early Music Movement” as a way of leaning into its complex and often problematic networks of mobility (e.g., across geographies and media) and the fault lines of its in(ex)clusion (e.g., considerations of [post]colonial performance practice). In this seminar we will explore such thematic vignettes as explorations of Early Music’s “modern” history and notions of revival, ideological debates regarding historically-informed performance practice, Early Music and alterity, and representations of the movement in film, among others.
